relevance_note: Single case report of a woman with a GFAP variant and Alexander disease: "a genetic test for AxD was ordered revealing a missense variation in the glial fibrillation acidic protein (GFAP) gene of p.Lys260Gln".
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; values typed by hand in a small Python script (no table transcription by script). Four rows in individuals: the patient; her mother (same variant on parental testing); the other parent, labelled 'parent of patient' because the paper says only 'Her parents were also tested' and names the mother as the carrier (sex and result for the other parent are not stated; no variant row); and the younger sister (reported by the parents to be beginning to show symptoms of dysautonomia; not tested). The mother's variant row uses the patient's printed variant plus the sentence 'the same mutation in her mother'; zygosity, type and pathogenicity left not reported for her because they are stated only for the patient's variant. Pathogenicity: the paper says the variant 'was classified as a “likely pathologic variant”', the Discussion says the findings 'strongly indicates that it is a pathogenic variant', and also that 'the one described earlier has not been proven to cause AxD' (possible internal inconsistency; recorded the classification as printed). In silico predictions (PROVEAN −3.49, conservation) are not functional assays, so functional_evidence_statement is not reported. Zygosity is not stated. Age 25 is given both as age at presentation and in 'a 25-year-old Caucasian female diagnosed with Alexander's disease'; used for both age at last evaluation and age at diagnosis. MRI 'high T2/FLAIR signal ... involving the subependymal periventricular tissue' was not mapped to 'periventricular rim' or 'cerebral white matter abnormality' (left not reported, as the paper does not name either); medulla/cervical cord atrophy observed. Mother's 'decreased balance and coordination' and 'difficulty regulating her temperature' are self-reported; not mapped to checklist ataxia or autonomic items. 'HEENT exam within normal limits' recorded as excluding only an abnormal HEENT exam. CSF viral tests and bone-marrow results not recorded as features. 'There are no other family members with these complaints' was not used to exclude features for the other parent or sister (unnamed group, and the next clause reports symptoms in the sister). First author surname taken as 'Zaver' from the header 'Zaver Dhillon B' by analogy with 'Douthit Nathan T'; uncertain.
